articles.summary: Microsoft has released updates to fix a record 169 security flaws, including a zero-day vulnerability in SharePoint that has been actively exploited. Among the patched issues are 157 rated Important and eight rated Critical, underscoring the widespread impact of this patch cycle.

articles.summary: Microsoft has released a substantial update patching 165 vulnerabilities, with over half of them being privilege escalation flaws. Notably, this release includes fixes for two zero-day exploits that were actively being used in the wild, highlighting the ongoing threat of unpatched vulnerabilities.

articles.summary: Microsoft's April 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses a significant number of vulnerabilities, including two zero-days and eight critical flaws among a total of 164 CVEs. This release underscores the ongoing challenges in software security and the importance of timely patching.

articles.title: ZionSiphon Malware Designed to Sabotage Water Treatment Systems
articles.summary: A new malware named ZionSiphon has been identified, specifically engineered to target and sabotage operational technology (OT) in water treatment and desalination facilities. The development of such specialized malware poses a critical threat to essential infrastructure and public safety.

articles.title: Critical NGINX Flaw Allows Configuration File Manipulation
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in nginx-ui allows attackers to abuse a near-maximum severity flaw to restart, create, modify, and delete NGINX configuration files. This could lead to complete server compromise and disruption of web services.

articles.title: Microsoft and Salesforce Patch AI Agent Data Leak Flaws
articles.summary: Microsoft and Salesforce have addressed critical prompt injection vulnerabilities in their AI agents, Copilot and Agentforce, respectively. These flaws could have allowed external attackers to exfiltrate sensitive data, underscoring the security challenges associated with AI integrations.

articles.title: Adobe Patches Actively Exploited Zero-Day in Acrobat and Reader
articles.summary: Adobe has issued a patch for a critical zero-day vulnerability in its Acrobat and Reader software that has been actively exploited for at least four months. Attackers were using specially crafted PDF files to compromise systems, emphasizing the danger of unpatched, exploited vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Industrial Controllers Still Vulnerable as Conflicts Move to Cyber

Research has identified 179 vulnerable operational technology (OT) devices, highlighting the increasing cyber threat to critical infrastructure.

articles.summary: A new paper examines how hackers perceive and discuss Artificial Intelligence, suggesting AI is seen as a significant innovation for cybercrime. The research indicates AI could amplify the scale and sophistication of attacks, impacting both novice and experienced cybercriminals.
